Specifically, independent claim 1 has been amended to recite a vehicle information acquisition unit configured to acquire vehicle information of the autonomous driving vehicle through communication with the autonomous driving vehicle in the parking place, the vehicle information includes a vehicle turning radius, a vehicle size, and a vehicle width of the autonomous driving vehicle and a parking plan generation unit configured to generate a parking plan and set the target parking space corresponding to the acquired vehicle information of the autonomous driving vehicle.

target parking space corresponding to the acquired vehicle information of the autonomous driving vehicle.

Support for these amendments may be found in the specification, figures and claims as originally filed, specifically, paragraphs [0033]-[0034] and [0037] of the application as filed. No subject matter has been disclaimed or abandoned and the amendment of certain claims is not to be construed as a dedication to the public of any of the subject matter of the claims as previously presented. No new matter has been entered through these amendments and entry is respectfully requested.

Claims 3, 5, and 9 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Tachibana. Claim 4 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Kim. Claim 6 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Bae and Kim. Claim 7 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Tachibana and Kim. Claim 8 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Bae and Tachibana. Claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Kim and Tachibana. Claim 12 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Shimamoto. Claim 13 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Bae and Shimamoto. Claims 14 and 16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Tachibana and Shimamoto. Claim 15 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Kim and Shimamoto. The rejections are respectfully traversed.

For a prior art reference to anticipate a claim, "the identical invention must be shown [in the prior art reference] in as complete detail as is contained in the claim." See MPEP 2131 (quoting Richardson v. Suzuki Motor Co., 868 F.2d 1226, 1236 (Fed. Cir. 1989)). A claim may be anticipated by a prior art reference "only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently described, in a single prior art reference." Id. (quoting Verdegaal Bros. v. Union Oil Co. of California, 814 F.2d 628, 631 (Fed. Cir. 1987)).

The rationale to support a conclusion that the claim would have been obvious is that all the claimed elements were known in the prior art and one skilled in the art could have combined the elements as claimed by known methods with no change in their respective functions, and the combination yielded nothing more than predictable results to one of ordinary skill in the art. KSR, 550 U.S. at 416, 82 USPQ2d at 1395; Sakraida v. AG Pro, Inc., 425 U.S. 273, 282, 189 USPQ 449, 453 (1976); Anderson's-Black Rock, Inc. v. Pavement Salvage Co., 396 U.S. 57, 62- 63, 163 USPQ 673, 675 (1969); Great Atl. & P. Tea Co. v. Supermarket Equip. Corp., 340 U.S. 147, 152, 87 USPQ 303, 306 (1950). Further, "a prior art reference must be considered in its entirety, i.e., as a whole, including portions that would lead away from the claimed invention." W.L. Gore & Assoc., Inc. v. Garlock, Inc., 721 F.2d 1540, 220 USPQ 303 (Fed. Cir. 1983), cert. denied, 469 U.S. 851 (1984).

Applicant respectfully submits that Cho fails to expressly or inherently disclose, teach, and/or fairly suggest each and every feature of amended independent claim 1. Specifically, Applicant submits that Cho fails to expressly or inherently disclose, teach, and/or fairly suggest the features regarding a vehicle information acquisition unit configured to acquire vehicle information of the autonomous driving vehicle through communication with the autonomous driving vehicle in the parking place, the vehicle information includes a vehicle turning radius, a vehicle size, and a vehicle width of the autonomous driving vehicle and a parking plan generation unit configured to generate a parking plan and set the target parking space corresponding to the acquired vehicle information of the autonomous driving vehicle.

Applicant respectfully submits that Cho fails to expressly or inherently disclose, teach, and/or fairly suggest each and every feature of amended independent claim 11. Specifically, Applicant submits that Cho fails to expressly or inherently disclose, teach, and/or fairly suggest the features regarding acquiring a vehicle information of the autonomous driving vehicle through communication with the autonomous driving vehicle in the parking place, the vehicle information includes a vehicle turning radius, a vehicle size, and a vehicle width of the autonomous driving vehicle and generating a parking plan and setting the target parking space corresponding to the acquired vehicle information of the autonomous driving vehicle.
In the rejection, the Examiner takes the position that Cho discloses every feature of independent claims 1 and 11.

However, in sharp contrast, Cho fails to disclose whatsoever that vehicle information acquired through communication with the autonomous driving vehicle in the parking place includes a vehicle turning radius, a vehicle size, and a vehicle width of the autonomous driving vehicle and based on the acquired vehicle information, a parking plan is generated and the target parking space is set. Rather, Cho discloses in paragraph [0056]:

In step (3), an autonomous driving operation is performed in the parking lot. The autonomous driving of the vehicle includes driving, stopping, and resuming of driving. The autonomous driving of the vehicle is performed according to instructions transmitted from the infrastructure to the vehicle. Alternatively, the autonomous driving of the vehicle may be performed without relying on the instructions from the infrastructure. The vehicle can be autonomously self- driven to the target position along the guide route within a permitted driving area. During the driverless autonomous driving of the vehicle, the vehicle is controlled to drive at a preset speed or below.

This preset speed may be a value transmitted from the infrastructure to the vehicle or may be a value stored in the vehicle. In addition, the vehicle is controlled not to deviate beyond an error margin from the given guide route when driving along the guide route. This preset error margin may be a value transmitted from the infrastructure to the vehicle or may be a value stored in the vehicle. In addition, the vehicle may turn with a predetermined minimum turning radius when it is necessary to turn during the autonomous driving along the guide route. This preset minimum turning radius may be a value transmitted from the infrastructure to the vehicle or may be a value stored in the vehicle. The vehicle is controlled not to exceed a predetermined maximum acceleration value when autonomously driving along the guide route. This preset maximum acceleration value may be a value transmitted from the infrastructure to the vehicle or may be a value stored in the vehicle.
(Emphasis added)
Accordingly, Cho merely discloses that the predetermined turning radius may be used to control the vehicle along the guide route.
Applicant respectfully submits that Cho is silent to generating the given guide route based on the predetermined turning radius of the vehicle, vehicle size, and vehicle width.
Further, Applicant respectfully submits that Bae, Tachibana, Kim, and Shimamoto, either alone or in combination, fail to cure the defects of Cho, either alone or in combination.

Based on the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 1 and 11, and all claims which depend thereon, are not anticipated by or obvious in view of Cho. Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 1 and 11, are patentable over Cho. Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections be withdrawn and independent claims 1 and 11, and all claims that depend thereon, be held in a condition for allowance.

In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned to resolve efficiently any formal matters or to discuss any aspects of the application or of this response. Otherwise, early notification of allowable subject matter is respectfully requested.
